original_value: We present a multiattentive recurrent neural network architecture for automatic multilingual readability assessment. This architecture considers raw words as its main input, but internally captures text structure and informs its word attention process using other syntax- and morphology-related datapoints, known to be of great importance to readability. This is achieved by a multiattentive strategy that allows the neural network to focus on specific parts of a text for predicting its reading level. We conducted an exhaustive evaluation using data sets targeting multiple languages and prediction task types, to compare the proposed model with traditional, state-of-the-art, and other neural network strategies.

result.paraphrase: We introduce a multiattentive recurrent neural network architecture for automatic multilingual readability assessment. While the model takes raw words as its primary input, it internally captures text structure and guides word attention with additional syntax- and morphology-related signals, which are known to be highly important for readability. This is accomplished through a multiattentive approach that lets the network concentrate on specific text segments when predicting reading level. We performed an exhaustive evaluation on datasets spanning multiple languages and task types to compare the proposed model with traditional methods, state-of-the-art systems, and other neural network approaches.
